text: Based on the medical history provided, Sara and her husband both have a family history of asthma, which significantly increases the likelihood that their baby has a genetic predisposition to developing asthma or other atopic conditions. The baby’s symptoms of wheezing and shortness of breath, particularly those occurring at night, are classic indicators of respiratory issues such as asthma, reactive airway disease, or other lower respiratory tract infections. Nighttime worsening of symptoms is a common characteristic of asthma due to natural circadian rhythms in airway tone and inflammation. Therefore, the primary health risk to assess is the development of childhood asthma or recurrent wheezing disorders. It is strongly recommended that the parents consult a pediatrician or a pediatric pulmonologist for a proper evaluation, which may include a physical exam, detailed history, and potentially diagnostic tests to determine the underlying cause of the wheezing and to establish an appropriate management plan.
